themes.name: Incentives Before Standards
themes.plain: Several problems stall because the person holding the answer gains nothing by sharing it, and nobody can make them. A shared standard or a central system cannot settle a fight over money, credit, or turf.
themes.evidence: On cross-channel journey orchestration all three models said the blocker is channel owners whose bonuses depend on their own volume and credited conversions; the same pattern appears in agentic traffic (agents gain by hiding), in the semantic context layer (teams keep definitions divergent on purpose), and in incrementality (platforms have no reason to expose how treatment was assigned).

themes.name: No Ground Truth to Measure Against
themes.plain: Many of these problems have no answer key to grade your work against, and the thing you measure often changes while you measure it. So the common first move is to build a small truth set of your own, or admit you are only estimating.
themes.evidence: Identity resolution answers say nobody has a verified list of who is the same person, answer engine optimization answers say replies are personalized and stochastic with no stable rank or denominator, B2B buying-group signal answers say few accounts ever buy so a dead signal and a fake one look alike, and content governance answers note expert reviewers disagree with each other.

themes.name: Chokepoint Before Trust
themes.plain: When the models cannot trust who is acting or what happens next, they build one door they own and push everything through it. A sent email or a spent dollar cannot be taken back, so the only real control happens before the action leaves.
themes.evidence: Every agent execution answer builds a proxy, gateway, or control plane in front of martech APIs with hard spend and audience caps; downstream consent answers put one checkpoint on every path data leaves the warehouse, and journey orchestration answers route all sends through one shared contact ledger or pre-send eligibility check.

themes.name: Nobody Can Verify Downstream
themes.plain: Once data, money, or a message leaves your own systems, you cannot see inside the partner, ad platform, or trained model that now holds it. You can estimate whether the rules were honored, but you cannot prove it.
themes.evidence: Downstream consent answers call ad platforms and agency segments black boxes with no accepted test for removing someone from a trained model, incrementality answers say platforms control both the delivery and the evidence, and identity resolution answers say false matches inside closed platforms cannot be measured from outside.

themes.name: Judgment That Won't Compile
themes.plain: The hardest calls depend on meaning, context, and what a sentence implies, and no rule set fully captures that. The models end up shrinking human judgment into a smaller, safer box rather than removing it.
themes.evidence: Content governance answers agree that deciding whether evidence supports a claim is a contextual judgment software cannot defend, so they limit what can be said; semantic layer answers say the meaning of "customer" is a political settlement, not a schema; and journey orchestration answers say there is no agreed definition of a good outcome to optimize.
